cim: BlackSky Adds AI Analytics to Space-Based Intelligence With EpochGeo Acquisition
cim_eredeti: BlackSky Adds AI Analytics to Space-Based Intelligence With EpochGeo Acquisition
szoveg_eredeti:
BlackSky Technology has acquired geospatial data science company EpochGeo to integrate artificial intelligence and machine learning analytics with its space-based intelligence services.

The Herndon, Virginia-based company disclosed the transaction Tuesday, saying EpochGeo’s technology combines radio frequency, signals intelligence and other data sources to support mission-critical national security and defense applications.

EpochGeo brings spatiotemporal AI/ML capabilities, data management tools and mission-specific, multi-source analytics to complement BlackSky’s satellite imagery services and support demand for integrated intelligence. BlackSky will continue serving EpochGeo’s existing customers, including major U.S. defense prime contractors and the federal government, through existing contracts.

BlackSky CEO Brian O’Toole said EpochGeo’s people and technology, along with its experience on customer missions, will help advance the company’s real-time intelligence work. He noted the firm has built and fielded analytics with end users in secure environments, including U.S. combatant commands and international defense ministries.

“These are exactly the capabilities our largest customers are asking us to provide as an integrated extension to real-time imaging services,” O’Toole said, noting that the next evolution of the industry is “the integration, fusion and analysis of a wide range of space-based and terrestrial data sources that enable us to rapidly see, understand and respond to relevant change in real-time.”

EpochGeo CEO Lou Paladino said his company supports government and commercial users through every stage of analytics work and the integration with BlackSky’s space-based intelligence will give customers a fuller view of the activities and trends shaping their operating environments.

BlackSky will build EpochGeo’s tools into its large data agreements and mission programs, offering them through its space-based intelligence and AI subscriptions or sovereign mission offerings.

The company expects the addition to help customers get more out of the imagery its satellites collect and to encourage wider use of its analytics services.

According to BlackSky, defense and security organizations worldwide are investing in satellite-based intelligence and want AI that can integrate diverse data sources to detect trends and forecast events before they happen.

BlackSky plans to grant restricted stock units covering up to 565,000 shares of its common stock to up to 43 EpochGeo employees in non-executive roles. Employees would receive the full share amount only if all 43 come on board.

The awards will be issued under an inducement equity plan that BlackSky’s board adopted on Oct. 29. Because the plan is limited to new hires, it did not require a shareholder vote under New York Stock Exchange rules.

Recipients who remain with BlackSky will see a quarter of their shares vest on Dec. 10, 2027. The remaining shares will vest quarterly in installments equal to one-sixteenth of the total award.

BlackSky’s existing government portfolio includes analytics support for U.S. military commands. In January 2025, the Space Force awarded the company multiple rapid procurement contracts to provide analytics services for tactical surveillance, reconnaissance and tracking, or TacSRT, missions. The services are offered through the Space Force’s online global data marketplace, which gives combatant commands access to BlackSky’s AI-driven analytics.

BlackSky fully acquired satellite manufacturer LeoStella in November 2024 by purchasing the remaining 50 percent stake from Thales Alenia Space. LeoStella, which the two companies formed as a joint venture in 2018, builds BlackSky’s Gen-3 satellite, designed to use shortwave infrared imaging and inter-satellite links to deliver real-time information.

Earlier, the Navy awarded BlackSky a research contract to identify uses and capabilities for optical intersatellite link terminals on its Gen-3 imaging satellites. As part of the effort, the company is modifying its systems to accommodate a terminal aligned with the Space Development Agency’s Transport Layer and commercial transport layers.
